The game calculates Isaac's speed, range, tear delay, and damage before using them in Libra's balancing formula. This has the following notable effects:
If Isaac's Speed or Tear delay are already at their internal soft caps (2.00 and 5 respectively), items that increase them specifically will give no stats.
The only exception would be items that decrease tear delay, and then only if Isaac's tear delay isn't at the hard cap of 1.
If Isaac's tears stat has reached the soft cap corresponding to 5
, basic tears ups no longer add bonuses, only direct tear delay upgrades will. Likewise, direct fire rate increases have no effect if the absolute maximum of 120 has been reached.
Speed adjustments, despite the stat being bounded between 0.1 and 2.0, always have an effect.

Speed and range will positively scale as they increase; the higher these stats already are upon receiving a boost to either one, the bigger the boost to the rest of Isaac's stats. Range scales especially quickly, making large range upgrades like
and
very powerful with Libra.
Items that apply multipliers to Isaac's tear delay (
, etc.) can be fired more rapidly with less damage.
Damage upgrades become less effective. In return, speed and range upgrades now increase damage and tears.
Items that affect the stats of Isaac's tears after they're fired (
, etc.) do not go through the balancing formula and work as normal.

Libra's balancing formula values tear delay higher than the other stats and damage less than the other stats. This makes standard tears ups give more stats than a standard range or speed up, and standard damage ups give less stats than a standard range or speed up.

Generally speaking, if an item increases Isaac's damage per second, Isaac will receive a stat bonus. If the item lowers fire rate and increases damage, or vice versa, in a way that results in loss of DPS, Isaac's stats will go down.
Since tear falling speed is not involved in the calculations, items such as
or
that increase tear falling speed but lower range are mostly detrimental.

\text{Charge Time} = \frac{1}{30}(Roundup(\text{Tear Delay} \times 3) + 1) \approx \frac{3}{\text{Fire Rate}}

\text{Min Charge Damage per Tick} = \text{Damage} \times \frac{5}{4}(\text{Fire Rate} \times (Roundup(\text{Tear Delay}) + 1) - 10)
At 30.00 fire rate or above (0 tear delay or lower), charging is no longer needed and fires 30 rings per second. Higher fire rate results in higher laser damage.

Despite being described as a 25% chance, whether a pedestal disappears is determined by its InitSeed.

The result can be predicted by applying a 32-bit xorshift to the InitSeed with shifts 5, 27, and 8. If the resulting unsigned value is less than 230 (1,073,741,824), the pedestal disappears; otherwise, it is rerolled.

InitSeeds 8, 41, 74, 107, 140, and 173 are observed edge cases that also cause the pedestal to disappear. Including these edge cases, the actual probability is slightly higher than 25%: approximately 25.0000014%.
